title: Prosecution asks ICC chamber to reject Rodrigo Duterte defense request on evidence
summary: Prosecutors asked the International Criminal Court Trial Chamber III to dismiss a request of former president Rodrigo Duterte's defense team regarding evidentiary matters as they are procedurally…

blocks.text: Prosecutors asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) Pre-Trial Chamber III to dismiss a request of former president Rodrigo Duterte's defense team regarding evidentiary matters as they are procedurally improper.
In a public redacted document released November 20, the prosecutors argued that the defense's request contravenes the chamber's protocols on evidence.

"The Defence’s request to [REDACTED] goes well beyond the scope of the requested observations from the Chamber, namely, [REDACTED]. It also contravenes the Rules of Procedure and Evidence (the 'Rules') and the protocol established by the Chamber regarding challenges to the admissibility of evidence," the document read.

"While the Defence is clearly keen to [REDACTED], the Chamber has established a protocol regarding the submission of evidence, in accordance with rule 64(1) of the Rules, which requires that the parties 'raise issues as to admissibility of evidence, including on any of the standard evidentiary criteria, at the time when the evidence is submitted to the Chamber'," it added.
The prosecution added that the defense should raise its alleged concerns when the Prosecution actually submits the relevant evidence, rather than improperly couching its request inside observations.
"The Defence may therefore raise its alleged concerns [REDACTED] when it is submitted by the Prosecution instead of improperly couching the request in observations related to [REDACTED]," it said.
Moreover, the prosecutors also sought to correct a factual error made by the defense regarding specific statements central to the ongoing proceedings.

"The Prosecution also wishes to correct a mistaken submission made by the Defence. The Defence argues that [REDACTED]. However, the [REDACTED] at issue in these proceedings. The [REDACTED].[REDACTED].It is the [REDACTED]. Although [REDACTED]. The statements made by [REDACTED] at issue in these proceedings," the document further read.
The prosecutors' comments were submitted before Trial Chamber III judges Joanna Korner, Keebong Paek, and Nicolas Guillou.
The defense recently asked the chamber to reject the testimony of an ex-Davao City police officer, according to a public redacted filing released on November 18.

Duterte’s counsel Peter Haynes contested the admission of P-0002’s evidence, saying the articles invoked by the Office of the Prosecutor to collect and preserve it require proof that a witness can no longer testify orally.
“Absent such proof, the prior recorded testimony cannot be admitted and the witness must be called to give his evidence viva voce,” Haynes said.
The trial of Duterte for crimes against humanity will open on November 30, with judges first asking him whether he admits guilt or pleads not guilty.
The hearing will begin at 10 a.m. in The Hague (5 p.m. Philippine time).
The chamber earlier found Duterte fit to stand trial, stating that he “is able to effectively exercise his fair trial rights in the proceedings.”

Duterte was arrested in March 2025 at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 3 and is currently detained at the ICC Detention Centre in Scheveningen in The Hague, The Netherlands. —KG, GMA News
